title: HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (004) · Practice exam

format.note: The real exam is online proctored, 1 hour, with multiple choice questions (some with more than one correct answer). It tests Terraform 1.12. HashiCorp does not publish the number of questions.
format.scoring: HashiCorp does not publish the passing score. 70% here is an indicative target.

questions.q: What does Infrastructure as Code (IaC) mean?
o: Defining infrastructure in machine-readable configuration files that can be versioned, reviewed, and applied automatically
Writing application code that runs on servers
Configuring servers by hand through the cloud console
questions.e: IaC manages infrastructure through code instead of manual processes.

questions.q: Which are advantages of managing infrastructure with IaC?
o: Changes can be reviewed and versioned in source control
It removes the need to understand the underlying cloud services
It makes infrastructure free of charge
It guarantees that no human error is possible
questions.e: IaC improves consistency, reviewability, and repeatability; it does not replace knowledge of the platform.

questions.q: Terraform configuration is described as declarative. What does that mean?
o: You describe the desired end state, and Terraform works out the actions needed to reach it
You write the exact sequence of API calls to make
Terraform only reads infrastructure and never changes it
Configuration must be written in a general-purpose programming language
questions.e: Terraform compares desired state with current state and plans the required changes.

questions.q: A company uses AWS, Google Cloud, and an on-premises VMware environment. Why can Terraform help?
o: The same language and workflow can manage all of them through different providers
Terraform automatically migrates workloads between clouds
Terraform makes all clouds use the same API
Terraform only works with a single cloud per installation
questions.e: Providers translate the common workflow into each platform's API.

questions.q: Which statement about Terraform being 'service-agnostic' is correct?
o: Terraform can manage not only cloud infrastructure but also SaaS and other services, such as DNS, monitoring, and Git platforms, through providers
Terraform can only manage virtual machines
Terraform cannot manage services that have an API
Terraform requires every service to be from the same vendor
questions.e: Thousands of providers exist for many kinds of services.

questions.q: Applying the same Terraform configuration twice without changes produces no new changes the second time. Which IaC property is this?
questions.e: Terraform only proposes changes when the desired state differs from the current state.

questions.q: Why do teams typically store Terraform configuration in a version control system such as Git?
o: To track history, review changes through pull requests, and roll back to previous configurations
To store the state file safely
questions.e: Version control enables collaboration and auditing. The state file should be stored in a backend, not in Git.

questions.q: Compared to clicking in a cloud console, what is a key benefit of IaC for disaster recovery?
o: Infrastructure can be recreated quickly and consistently from code in another region or account
questions.e: Code describes the environment; data still needs its own backup strategy.

questions.q: Which of these is a tool whose primary purpose is provisioning infrastructure across many platforms, rather than configuring software inside existing servers?
questions.e: Terraform focuses on provisioning; configuration management tools such as Ansible focus on configuring systems.

questions.q: Where should you declare which providers a configuration needs and their acceptable versions?
o: In a required_providers block inside the terraform block
In the provider block with a version argument only
questions.e: required_providers declares source addresses and version constraints.

questions.q: What does the version constraint '~> 5.4' allow?
questions.e: The pessimistic operator allows the rightmost specified component to increment.

questions.q: What does the version constraint '~> 5.4.0' allow?
questions.e: With three components, only the patch version may increase.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the .terraform.lock.hcl file?
o: It records the exact provider versions and checksums selected, so every run uses the same versions
It locks the state during apply
It lists the modules to download
questions.e: The dependency lock file should be committed to version control.

questions.q: A colleague wants to move to a newer provider version allowed by the constraints, ignoring the version recorded in the lock file. Which command should they run?
questions.e: init -upgrade selects the newest versions allowed by constraints and updates the lock file.

questions.q: What is the source address of the official AWS provider?
questions.e: Provider source addresses have the form [hostname/]namespace/type; the default hostname is registry.terraform.io.

questions.q: How does Terraform interact with cloud platforms?
o: Through providers, plugins that translate Terraform resources into API calls for each platform
Through SSH connections to every server
By editing the cloud provider's database directly
questions.e: Providers implement resource types and data sources.

questions.q: You need to create resources in two AWS regions in the same configuration. What should you do?
o: Define two provider blocks, one with an alias, and set provider = aws.ALIAS on the resources of the second region
Run Terraform twice with different environment variables
It is not possible in one configuration
questions.e: Aliases allow multiple configurations of the same provider.

questions.q: Which statement about provider plugins is correct?
o: terraform init downloads the required providers into the working directory (or uses a plugin cache)
Providers are built into the Terraform binary
Providers are downloaded during terraform apply
Providers must be compiled from source by the user
questions.e: Providers are separate plugins installed during init.

questions.q: A configuration uses the AWS, Kubernetes, and Helm providers together. Which statements are correct?
o: Each provider is declared in required_providers and configured with its own provider block
Resources of different providers can reference each other's attributes
Only one provider can be used per configuration
Providers must all come from the same company
Using multiple providers requires HCP Terraform
questions.e: Cross-provider references are common, for example passing a cluster endpoint to the Kubernetes provider.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of Terraform state?
o: To map resources in the configuration to real-world objects and track metadata
To store the source code of modules
questions.e: State binds configuration to real resources and improves performance.

questions.q: Which statement about secrets in Terraform state is correct?
o: State can contain sensitive values in plain text, so it must be stored securely, for example in an encrypted remote backend with restricted access
Terraform never writes sensitive values to state
Marking a variable sensitive removes it from state
State is always encrypted by Terraform itself
questions.e: sensitive = true only hides values in CLI output.

questions.q: Where does Terraform store state by default if no backend is configured?
o: In a terraform.tfstate file in the working directory (local backend)
questions.e: The local backend is the default.

questions.q: Before refreshing or planning, why does Terraform compare state with the real infrastructure?
o: To detect changes made outside Terraform and propose actions based on the current situation
questions.e: Plan refreshes state by default and then compares with the configuration.

questions.q: Can you use a provider that is not published by HashiCorp?
o: Yes, partner and community providers are published in the Terraform Registry with their own namespaces
No, only HashiCorp providers are allowed
Only if it is written in HCL
questions.e: The Registry contains official, partner, and community providers.

questions.q: Which statement about provider-defined functions is correct?
o: Since Terraform 1.8 providers can offer functions called with the syntax provider::NAME::FUNCTION
Users can define their own functions in HCL
Functions can only come from modules
questions.e: Terraform does not support user-defined functions in HCL, but providers can contribute functions.

questions.q: What is the core Terraform workflow?
questions.e: Write configuration, preview changes with plan, and apply them.

questions.q: Which command must you run first in a new working directory, or after adding a provider or module?
questions.e: init configures the backend and installs providers and modules.

questions.q: What does terraform init do?
questions.e: init prepares the working directory; it does not create infrastructure.

questions.q: What does terraform validate check?
o: That the configuration is syntactically valid and internally consistent, without contacting remote services
That the plan has no changes
That the cloud credentials are valid
That the state matches real infrastructure
questions.e: validate is useful in CI; it requires an initialized directory but does not access remote state or APIs.

questions.q: You want to save a plan and apply exactly that plan later in the pipeline. Which commands do this?
o: terraform plan -out=tfplan and then terraform apply tfplan
terraform plan > tfplan and terraform apply < tfplan
questions.e: Applying a saved plan does not prompt and does not recalculate.

questions.q: What does terraform apply do when run without a saved plan?
o: It creates a new plan, shows it, and asks for confirmation before applying
It fails because a plan file is required
questions.e: Use -auto-approve to skip confirmation, typically only in automation.

questions.q: A plan shows '-/+' next to a resource. What does it mean?
o: The resource will be destroyed and recreated (replaced)
The resource will be updated in place
The resource will be read only
questions.e: Replacement happens when an argument that cannot be updated in place changes.

questions.q: A plan shows '~' next to a resource. What does it mean?
o: The resource will be updated in place
The resource will be moved to another state
questions.e: + create, - destroy, ~ update in place, -/+ replace.

questions.q: Which command destroys all resources managed by the current configuration and state?
questions.e: destroy is an alias for terraform apply -destroy.

questions.q: You want to preview what terraform destroy would do without destroying anything. What should you run?
questions.e: plan -destroy creates a speculative destroy plan.

questions.q: A virtual machine is misbehaving and you want Terraform to recreate it on the next apply, although the configuration did not change. What is the recommended way?
o: terraform taint ADDRESS (the preferred modern way)
terraform destroy -target with no further step
questions.e: -replace replaced the deprecated taint command.

questions.q: What does terraform fmt do?
o: Rewrites configuration files to the canonical format and style
questions.e: Use fmt -check in CI and -recursive for subdirectories.

questions.q: In a CI pipeline, you want the job to fail if any file is not formatted, without changing files. Which command?
questions.e: -check returns a non-zero exit code if formatting is needed.

questions.q: When should -target be used with plan or apply?
o: Only in exceptional situations, such as recovering from errors, because it can leave configuration and state inconsistent
To speed up all applies in production
To apply changes to multiple workspaces
questions.e: HashiCorp recommends using -target only for exceptional circumstances.

questions.q: Which options make terraform plan exit with a code that distinguishes 'no changes' from 'changes present', useful in automation?
questions.e: Exit code 0 no changes, 1 error, 2 changes present.

questions.q: In automation, you want Terraform to fail instead of prompting for missing variable values. Which flag?
questions.e: -input=false disables interactive prompts.

questions.q: Which statements about terraform plan are correct?
o: It does not change real infrastructure
It refreshes the state in memory by default to compare it with the configuration
It permanently deletes resources removed from configuration
It is required before every terraform destroy
questions.e: Plan is a preview; apply makes changes.

questions.q: Which style conventions does HashiCorp recommend?
o: Two-space indentation and aligned equals signs, as produced by terraform fmt
Use snake_case names for resources and variables
Put all configuration in a single line
questions.e: See the style guide.

questions.q: What happens to resources when you remove their block from the configuration and run terraform apply?
o: Nothing, they are kept and forgotten
They are moved to another state
questions.e: To stop managing without destroying, use a removed block with destroy = false.

questions.q: Which command shows a human-readable version of a saved plan file or of the current state?
questions.e: terraform show can also produce JSON with -json.

questions.q: What does 'terraform apply -refresh-only' do?
o: Updates the state to match real infrastructure without changing infrastructure
Applies only to resources marked refresh
questions.e: It replaced the deprecated terraform refresh command.

questions.q: What is the difference between a resource block and a data block?
o: A resource creates and manages an object; a data source only reads information about an existing object
Data blocks create objects; resources only read
Data blocks are only for variables
questions.e: Data sources let configuration use information defined elsewhere.

questions.q: You need the ID of the latest Ubuntu AMI published by Canonical to use in an aws_instance. What should you use?
o: A data source such as aws_ami with filters
A local value with a hard-coded ID forever
questions.e: Data sources query existing objects.

questions.q: How do you reference the id attribute of resource aws_vpc named main?
questions.e: Resource references use TYPE.NAME.ATTRIBUTE.

questions.q: How do you reference an attribute of a data source aws_caller_identity named current?
questions.e: Data sources are referenced with the data. prefix.

questions.q: Which statement about implicit dependencies is correct?
o: When a resource references another resource's attribute, Terraform creates them in the correct order automatically
Terraform creates resources in the order they appear in files
Every dependency must be declared with depends_on
Dependencies are only supported inside modules
questions.e: Terraform builds a dependency graph from references.

questions.q: When should you use depends_on?
o: When a dependency exists that Terraform cannot infer from references, for example a hidden dependency on an IAM policy
questions.e: depends_on is a last resort for hidden dependencies.

questions.q: Several values are provided for the same input variable. Which source has the HIGHEST precedence?
questions.e: Order (lowest to highest): environment variables, terraform.tfvars, terraform.tfvars.json, *.auto.tfvars, then -var/-var-file in order given.

questions.q: Which source has the LOWEST precedence for input variable values (besides the default)?
questions.e: Environment variables are evaluated first and overridden by files and CLI flags.

questions.q: How is the value of 'variable "region" {}' set through an environment variable?
questions.e: Terraform reads TF_VAR_ followed by the variable name.

questions.q: What does 'sensitive = true' on an output do?
o: Hides the value in CLI output, but the value is still stored in state
Prevents other modules from using it
questions.e: Protect the state itself.

questions.q: Which command prints a single output value without quotes, useful in shell scripts?
questions.e: -json prints all outputs as JSON.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a locals block?
o: To name expressions so they can be reused in a module without repeating them
To export values to other configurations
questions.e: Local values are like a function's temporary variables.

questions.q: Which type constraint describes a value like {name = "web", port = 80}, with named attributes of different types?
questions.e: Objects have a fixed set of named attributes, each with its own type.

questions.q: What is the difference between a list and a set?
o: A list is ordered and allows duplicates; a set is unordered and contains unique values
A set is ordered; a list is not
questions.e: for_each accepts sets of strings or maps.

questions.q: Which statement about a tuple type is correct?
o: It is a sequence where each element can have a different, specific type, such as tuple([string, number])
It is an unordered collection of unique strings
It is a map with string keys
It is a type for secrets
questions.e: Tuples are structural types like objects, but positional.

questions.q: You need to create one IAM user for each name in var.users (a set of strings) and later remove a user in the middle without affecting the others. What should you use?
questions.e: With count, removing an element in the middle shifts indices and causes replacements; for_each uses stable keys.

questions.q: What can for_each iterate over in a resource block?
o: A map or a set of strings
questions.e: Convert a list with toset() if needed.

questions.q: What does a dynamic block do?
o: Generates repeated nested blocks (such as ingress rules) from a collection
questions.e: Dynamic blocks are for nested blocks inside a resource; overuse reduces readability.

questions.q: Which expression returns a list of the ids of all instances created with count in aws_instance.web?
questions.e: The splat expression collects an attribute from every element.

questions.q: Which expression creates a resource only when var.enabled is true?
questions.e: Conditional expressions are often used with count.

questions.q: Which expression transforms a list of names into a list of uppercase names?
questions.e: for expressions transform collections.

questions.q: Which tool lets you experiment with expressions and functions interactively?
questions.e: terraform console evaluates expressions against the current state.

questions.q: Which function calculates a subnet address range from a VPC CIDR, such as the third /24 in 10.0.0.0/16?
questions.e: cidrsubnet(prefix, newbits, netnum).

questions.q: Which function renders a file with variables, such as a cloud-init script?
questions.e: file() reads a file as-is; templatefile() renders a template.

questions.q: Which function combines two maps, with values of the second overriding the first?
questions.e: concat works on lists; merge on maps or objects.

questions.q: You want to reject values of var.environment other than dev, staging, or prod before any plan is computed. What should you add?
o: A validation block in the variable, with condition and error_message
questions.e: Variable validation runs when values are assigned.

questions.q: What happens when a check block assertion fails?
o: Terraform reports a warning, but the plan or apply continues
The apply is blocked and rolled back
questions.e: Check blocks validate infrastructure without blocking operations; preconditions and postconditions block.

questions.q: You want apply to fail if the AMI selected by a data source is not for x86_64 architecture, before creating the instance. What should you use?
o: A precondition in the lifecycle block of the resource
questions.e: Preconditions are evaluated before the resource is planned; postconditions after.

questions.q: Which lifecycle arguments exist?
questions.e: replace_triggered_by, precondition, and postcondition also exist in lifecycle.

questions.q: Tags on an instance are modified by an external tool and you do not want Terraform to revert them. What should you add?
questions.e: ignore_changes tells Terraform to ignore differences for those attributes.

questions.q: A database must never be destroyed accidentally by Terraform. What should you add?
questions.e: Plans that would destroy the resource fail with an error.

questions.q: Which practices reduce the risk of leaking secrets with Terraform?
o: Read secrets at runtime from a secrets manager such as Vault instead of hard-coding them
Use ephemeral resources and write-only arguments, which are not persisted in plan or state
Commit terraform.tfvars with passwords to Git
Store state in a public bucket
questions.e: Since Terraform 1.10/1.11, ephemeral values and write-only arguments help keep secrets out of state.

questions.q: Which statement about ephemeral resources is correct?
o: They provide temporary values, such as a secret read from Vault, that Terraform never stores in plan or state
They are resources destroyed after each apply
They are the same as data sources
They are only available in HCP Terraform
questions.e: Ephemeral resources were introduced in Terraform 1.10.

questions.q: Which statement about 'sensitive = true' on a variable is correct?
o: Terraform redacts the value in plan and apply output, but it can still be stored in state
The value is not stored anywhere
The value is encrypted with Vault
The value cannot be used in resources
questions.e: Use ephemeral values to avoid persistence.

questions.q: What is a Terraform module?
o: A container for multiple resources used together; every configuration has at least the root module
questions.e: Modules organize and reuse configuration.

questions.q: Which module sources does Terraform support?
o: The Terraform Registry and private registries
questions.e: HTTP URLs and object storage (S3, GCS) are also supported.

questions.q: When can you use the version argument in a module block?
o: When the module comes from a module registry (public or private)
With any source, including local paths
questions.e: For Git sources, pin a version with ?ref=tag.

questions.q: How do you pin a module from a Git repository to the tag v1.3.0?
questions.e: The ref query parameter selects a branch, tag, or commit.

questions.q: What is the source format of a public Terraform Registry module?
questions.e: Registry modules use a three-part address.

questions.q: A child module needs the VPC ID created in the root module. How do you pass it?
o: Declare an input variable in the child module and set it in the module block
The child module automatically sees all root resources
Reference aws_vpc.main directly in the child module
questions.e: Modules only see their own variables, locals, and resources.

questions.q: How does the root module use a value created inside a child module named network?
o: The child module declares an output, and the root references module.network.OUTPUT_NAME
questions.e: Outputs are the interface of a module.

questions.q: After adding a new module block, which command must you run before plan?
o: terraform init (or terraform get) to install the module
questions.e: Modules are installed in .terraform/modules.

questions.q: A child module needs to use a non-default provider configuration, such as aws.west. How do you pass it?
o: Use the providers argument in the module block: providers = { aws = aws.west }
Declare a new provider block with credentials inside the module
Set the region with an environment variable only
questions.e: Reusable modules should not contain provider configurations; they receive them from the caller.

questions.q: Which statement about module input variables and scope is correct?
o: Variables declared in a module are only accessible inside that module
Variables of the root module are automatically visible in all child modules
Child module variables can be set with TF_VAR_ directly
Outputs of a module are global
questions.e: Each module has its own namespace.

questions.q: Which practices are recommended when consuming modules from a registry?
o: Pin versions with constraints and upgrade deliberately
Review the module's inputs, outputs, and documentation
Always use the latest version without constraints in production
questions.e: Pinning avoids unexpected changes.

questions.q: Can you use count or for_each on a module block?
o: Yes, to create multiple instances of a module
questions.e: Module instances are referenced as module.NAME[KEY].

questions.q: Where can a company publish modules for internal use only, with versioning?
o: The HCP Terraform private registry (or a Git repository with tags)
questions.e: Private registries support versions and discovery.

questions.q: What is the recommended minimal structure of a reusable module?
o: main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, and a README
questions.e: This is the standard module structure.

questions.q: What is the default backend and where does it store state?
o: The local backend, in terraform.tfstate on the local filesystem
The remote backend in a Git repository
questions.e: Local state is fine for learning but not for teams.

questions.q: Why is local state a problem for a team?
o: Each person has a different copy, there is no locking, and the file may be lost or contain secrets on laptops
questions.e: Remote backends provide shared state, locking, and protection.

questions.q: What is the purpose of state locking?
o: To prevent two operations from writing to the same state at the same time
To prevent resources from being destroyed
questions.e: Locking happens automatically on supported backends for operations that write state.

questions.q: A previous run crashed and the state lock remained. After verifying no other run is active, what should you do?
questions.e: force-unlock removes a stuck lock; use with care.

questions.q: Which statement about the backend block is correct?
o: It cannot use input variables or locals; values can be supplied with partial configuration via -backend-config
questions.e: Backend configuration is evaluated before variables.

questions.q: With the S3 backend in recent Terraform versions, how can state locking be enabled without DynamoDB?
o: use_lockfile = true, which uses S3 native lock files
questions.e: S3 native locking was introduced in Terraform 1.10; DynamoDB-based locking is deprecated.

questions.q: You changed the backend configuration from local to a remote backend. What should you run?
questions.e: init detects the change and offers to migrate state.

questions.q: Which backend supports state locking natively in Google Cloud?
o: local on a shared NFS disk
questions.e: The gcs backend supports locking.

questions.q: Another team's configuration needs the VPC ID output by your configuration. What can they use?
o: The terraform_remote_state data source (or, better, a data source of the provider or a shared parameter store)
Copy your state file into their repository
questions.e: terraform_remote_state reads root module outputs; it requires read access to the whole state.

questions.q: What is resource drift?
o: A difference between real infrastructure and what Terraform's state and configuration expect, often caused by manual changes
A module moved to another folder
questions.e: Drift is detected during refresh and plan.

questions.q: Someone changed a security group manually. You want to accept the change into state without modifying infrastructure, then update the code. What do you run?
questions.e: refresh-only updates state to match reality; then align the configuration.

questions.q: Someone changed a security group manually, and you want to restore the configuration's version. What do you do?
o: Run terraform plan and apply: Terraform proposes changes to bring the resource back to the configuration
questions.e: A normal plan detects drift and reverts it.

questions.q: What are CLI workspaces in Terraform Community Edition?
o: Separate state instances for the same configuration and backend, such as default and test
questions.e: terraform.workspace returns the current workspace name.

questions.q: Which commands manage CLI workspaces?
questions.e: list, show, and delete also exist.

questions.q: Which flag reconfigures the backend ignoring existing configuration, without migrating state?
questions.e: -reconfigure disregards saved backend configuration.

questions.q: Should the state file be committed to Git?
o: No: it can contain secrets and conflicts arise; use a remote backend
Only the lock file of state
questions.e: Commit .terraform.lock.hcl, not terraform.tfstate.

questions.q: Existing resources were created manually. You want Terraform to manage them with a reviewable, plannable process. What is recommended?
o: Add import blocks with the resource address and id, then run plan and apply
questions.e: Import blocks (Terraform 1.5+) make import part of the plan workflow.

questions.q: You have import blocks but no resource configuration yet. Which command can generate it for you?
questions.e: Generated configuration should be reviewed and cleaned.

questions.q: Which command lists all resources tracked in the state?
questions.e: state show ADDRESS displays one resource's attributes.

questions.q: You renamed a resource in configuration from aws_instance.web to aws_instance.app. How do you avoid Terraform destroying and recreating it?
o: Add a moved block from aws_instance.web to aws_instance.app
questions.e: moved blocks are reviewable; terraform state mv also works but is not in code.

questions.q: You want Terraform to stop managing a resource without destroying it. What is the declarative way?
o: A removed block with lifecycle { destroy = false }
Delete the resource from the cloud console
questions.e: terraform state rm is the imperative alternative.

questions.q: Which commands inspect state without modifying it?
questions.e: rm and mv modify state.

questions.q: Terraform behaves unexpectedly and you need detailed logs. What do you set?
o: TF_LOG=DEBUG (or TRACE) and optionally TF_LOG_PATH to write logs to a file
questions.e: Levels: TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR; JSON outputs TRACE in JSON.

questions.q: You suspect a problem in a provider, not in Terraform core. How can you increase logging only for providers?
questions.e: TF_LOG_CORE and TF_LOG_PROVIDER control the two components separately.

questions.q: Which command outputs the dependency graph in DOT format?
questions.e: The output can be rendered with Graphviz.

questions.q: With import blocks, can you import several resources using for_each?
o: Yes, since Terraform 1.7 import blocks support for_each
Only with the CLI terraform import
questions.e: This simplifies importing many similar resources.

questions.q: What should you do after importing resources?
o: Run terraform plan and adjust configuration until plan shows no unexpected changes
Delete the import blocks before apply
Commit the state file to Git
questions.e: Import brings objects into state; configuration must match them.

questions.q: What is HCP Terraform?
o: HashiCorp's managed service that runs Terraform remotely with shared state, collaboration, and governance features
A Terraform provider for HashiCorp products
questions.e: Formerly Terraform Cloud.

questions.q: How do you authenticate the Terraform CLI with HCP Terraform?
questions.e: login obtains an API token and stores it in the CLI credentials file.

questions.q: Which block connects a configuration to HCP Terraform for CLI-driven runs?
o: The cloud block inside the terraform block, with organization and workspaces
questions.e: The cloud block replaced the remote backend as the preferred integration.

questions.q: In HCP Terraform, what does a workspace contain?
o: The state, variables, run history, and settings for one configuration's infrastructure
questions.e: HCP Terraform workspaces differ from CLI workspaces.

questions.q: How are HCP Terraform workspaces grouped to organize permissions and settings?
questions.e: Projects group workspaces; teams can be granted access per project.

questions.q: Which run workflows does HCP Terraform support?
o: VCS-driven (runs triggered by commits and pull requests)
CLI-driven (terraform plan/apply from the local CLI, executed remotely)
questions.e: API-driven runs are also supported.

questions.q: In a VCS-driven workspace, what happens when a pull request is opened?
o: HCP Terraform runs a speculative plan and reports the result on the pull request
questions.e: Speculative plans cannot be applied.

questions.q: Which HCP Terraform features help enforce organization rules on every run, for example forbidding public buckets?
o: Policy enforcement with Sentinel or OPA policy sets
Run tasks integrating external tools such as security scanners
questions.e: Policies and run tasks are part of governance.

questions.q: Several workspaces need the same cloud credentials and common variables. What is the simplest way to share them?
o: Variable sets applied to multiple workspaces or projects
questions.e: Variable sets reduce duplication.

questions.q: How should HCP Terraform authenticate to AWS or Google Cloud without static long-lived keys?
o: Dynamic provider credentials using workload identity (OIDC)
Store access keys in a public variable
Commit credentials to the VCS repository
questions.e: Dynamic credentials are short-lived and scoped per run.

questions.q: Which feature lets HCP Terraform detect when real infrastructure has drifted from state, on a schedule?
questions.e: Health assessments run checks and drift detection periodically.

questions.q: Infrastructure is in a private network that HCP Terraform cannot reach. What allows runs to execute there?
o: HCP Terraform agents installed in the private network
A public IP on every resource
questions.e: Agents poll HCP Terraform and execute runs inside your network.

questions.q: How are access permissions to workspaces managed in HCP Terraform?
o: Through teams with permissions on organizations, projects, and workspaces
questions.e: Teams group users and receive permissions.

questions.q: What does remote execution mode mean for a workspace?
o: Plans and applies run on HCP Terraform's infrastructure, and the CLI streams the output
Terraform runs only on the developer's laptop and stores nothing
Runs need to be manually copied
questions.e: In local execution mode HCP Terraform stores state only.
